newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rio's Banerj auction not expected until Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Rio's Banerj auction not expected until Thursday.

text.p: The privatization auction of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj is not expected to take place until Thursday as the sale still hinges on a Senate deal resolving Banerj's debts, officials said.
The Senate vote that would allow the state to sell the bank is not expected to take place until Thursday, according to Senate officials.

The Senate must approve a 2.9 billion reais loan from federal mortgage bank Caixa Economica Federal (CEF) to Rio de Janeiro state. The loan would cover all of Banerj's pension and payroll-related debts.
The Banerj auction, originally slated to take place on Tuesday, was rescheduled for 1000 local/1300 GMT Wednesday but is on hold because the Senate has not given its green light to the loan yet.
An aide to Senator Ney Suassuna, who is in charge of the issue in the Senate's Economic Affairs Committee, said the committee is likely to meet only Thursday in a extraordinary session.
The deal must be first approved by the Senate panel before it is put to a vote in the floor of the upper house.
The Rio de Janeiro state government is also appealing against a resolution issued by a labor court Tuesday that the new owners of Banerj would have to assume the bank's pension-related debts.
Four banks -- Bradesco, Banco Itau, BCN and Cia de Investimentos Latino-Americana, owned by an unidentified foreign bank and represented by local Banco Pactual -- signed up for Banerj auction.
Banerj, formally known as Banco Banerj S.A., is due to be sold at a minimum price of 310 million reais in a closed-envelope auction on the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange.
